_comment: Where hipointedemun's data wells are. Shape: cartograph/sources.js.
_why_two_wells: HiPointe–DeMun STRADDLES the City limit: Hi-Pointe is in St. Louis City, DeMun is in St. Louis County / City of Clayton. St. Louis City is an independent city, so its assessor holds no County parcels — two wells, complementary, and a field is absent for this scene only if BOTH lack it (which is why num_buildings/vacant/historic_district survive here on the city side).
_landUseCodes_why: The county well's LUCODE is numeric and opaque; the CSV is the assessor's own decode table, published alongside the parcel layer and re-acquired per jurisdiction.
_history_why: content/nr-inventory.json is the building inventory of the National Register nomination NRHP 05000370, OCR'd; each matched building carries its NR facts (contributing, style, date) and the nomination's reference. ⛔ No district membership is derived from it (Boz, 2026-10-26, on Jacob's 2026-10-21 ruling): the former historicDistricts declaration (name, nomination streets, Richmond Heights exclusion) was removed with the MHC well.
_state_wells: The wells are taken from the state record (cartograph/states/mo.mjs) and resolved by cartograph/sources.js; this file declares only what the town takes and how it selects.
_cropland_why: USDA's national Cropland Data Layer (cartograph/cdl.mjs): crop rows grow where OSM maps a field and, where it maps none, where the CDL reads crop (Jacob, 2026-10-05). 2024 is the latest year fetched.
